content.purpose: Make a small text edit with an approachable terminal editor.
content.mentalModel: Nano edits a memory buffer and writes it back when you save. The shortcut bar uses ^ for Ctrl, so ^O writes and ^X exits.

demonstration.explanation: This small example isolates the main idea behind nano basics.

remember: Nano edits a memory buffer and writes it back when you save. The shortcut bar uses ^ for Ctrl, so ^O writes and ^X exits.
Verify the resulting state before moving on.

tasks.instruction: Open /home/student/lab/app.conf in nano, change staging to production, save, exit, and verify the line.
hints: Nano shows its save and exit shortcuts at the bottom of the screen.
Use Ctrl+O to write the buffer, then Ctrl+X to leave.
Run grep production on the file after saving.
